answer: A web of trust stops cheap copies the way a flock trusts only familiar wings: a new agent cannot earn until established agents vouch for it, like a sparrow accepted into a roost only after known birds sing for it. Each voucher stakes its own reputation, so if the newcomer cheats, its sponsors lose standing and future rewards. Crossing a dune of fake identities therefore costs real social capital, not just new accounts, and an attacker would need to corrupt an ocean of trusted relationships before a single forgery could profit.
